# Node-Level Uncertainty Estimation in LLM-Generated SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#node-level-uncertainty)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-10**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.lrec-1.168.pdf) · LREC 2026 proceedings, pages 2145–2153

**Reading coverage:** All nine PDF pages: Sections 1–4, conclusions and limitations, Algorithm 1, Tables 1–2, the AST example, references and all 13 Appendix A examples. Table 1 visually inspected.

## Research question

Locate suspect components in generated SQL instead of assigning one confidence score to the entire query.

## Method

A reference-AST alignment heuristic normalizes aliases and operator symmetry, suppresses blame on containers and globally rescues matching nodes. A LightGBM classifier uses 72 structural, lexical and schema features without reference SQL at inference.

## Evaluation

OmniSQL-7B generates BIRD development candidates and 67,901 SynSQL candidates from 453 databases. Experiments compare query splits within databases, three held-out BIRD databases, and SynSQL-to-BIRD transfer using node-level ROC-AUC against heuristic labels.

## What the results support

Overall ROC-AUC is 76.51% in-database, 69.46% across BIRD databases and 66.47% after SynSQL training. Aggregate discrimination exceeds mean token log-probabilities, but not every node type improves; Table nodes are slightly worse in the first experiment.

## Limits and qualifications

Labels encode a comparison convention rather than full natural-language correctness. Missing predicates or other omitted clauses are intentionally unlabelled. Thirteen prototyping cases are not an independent label-quality audit. Only one SQL generator is evaluated, and ROC-AUC does not establish calibrated probabilities or useful downstream abstention.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A localized error-confidence baseline for verification and targeted review; direct ambiguity detection, clarification, repair effectiveness and selective-risk control remain untested.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Claim or inference examined | Original evidence | Location | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The reported uncertainty probabilities are empirically calibrated. | Section 1 interprets uncertainty as calibrated probability, while Section 4 and both result tables report ROC-AUC without calibration-error, reliability-diagram or proper-scoring evaluation. | Section 1; Section 4/Tables 1–2 | Support error ranking, not demonstrated probability calibration. |
| No erroneous generated nodes means a complete correct query. | Remark 2 excludes omissions, and Appendix A Example 6 gives no incorrect nodes when ORDER BY is absent from the generated query. | Section 3.1/Remark 2; Appendix A Example 6 | Node labels do not assess query completeness or general semantic correctness. |
| The headline 27.44% gain is a relative improvement across all settings. | Table 1 aggregate AUC values are 76.51% and 49.07%, a 27.44-percentage-point difference in the in-database experiment; Table 2 has different cross-database/transfer values. | Abstract; Table 1; Table 2 | Use percentage points and the specific evaluation condition. |
